Subject: Data geography / retention questions for hosted API

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for taking this. We're working through the security questionnaire and have a few specific asks about Redwood's hosted API behavior for PA/PII and transaction traces: 

1) Where is customer data physically stored by default (region/locations)? Can we require EU-only residency for our project?
2) How long are request payloads, generated outputs, and associated logs retained for (break out by transient logs, audit logs, backups)?
3) If we request deletion for a tenant (or an API key), what is the end-to-end timeline and what artifacts remain (backups, audit trails)?
4) Are backups encrypted and what is the retention / overwrite policy for backups?
5) Can you provide the customer-facing phrasing we can include in our internal security questionnaire (short answer + one-paragraph explanation)?

We'd like to share your answers with our security and legal teams — small follow-up if anything needs a redline.

Appreciate it,
Alice Johnson

Quick draft answers (high level):
- Default storage region: customer-configurable; default is us-west-2 for new signups but EU-only residency is available for accounts requesting EU tenancy.
- Retention: request/response payloads and short-term debug logs retained for 30 days by default; audit logs retained 365 days; backups retained 90 days (configurable for enterprise).
- Deletion: deletion requests trigger a purge workflow; primary data removed within 7 days, backups overwritten per backup retention windows (up to 90 days), and an audit record of the deletion is kept for compliance.
- Encryption: data at rest and in transit encrypted; backups encrypted with customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and Redwood-managed KMS for hosted by default.

Rafael / Alice —

Thanks for the draft. I've reviewed and tightened the operational details below — this is safe to share with Stellar's security team as-is; where there are customer-choice knobs I call them out explicitly.

Authoritative answers:
1) Region / residency: Hosted accounts are deployed to a single region chosen at account creation. For new hosted customers we can provision EU-only residency (data and backups kept exclusively in eu-west-1) — this requires an account-level configuration and SLA addendum. Cross-region replication for disaster recovery is opt-in and documented in the contract.

2) Retention windows (default hosted plan):
- Request payloads (full request body) and model outputs: retained for 30 days to support debugging, abuse detection, and quality monitoring. This is configurable for enterprise customers; some customers choose shorter windows or request dedicated in-region retention limits.
- Short-term diagnostic logs (aggregated traces): retained 30 days.
- Audit logs (API key usage, administrative actions): retained 365 days and immutable for compliance investigations.
- Backups (snapshot of persisted inference metadata/config): retained 90 days by default; encrypted and stored in region of record.

3) Deletion / erasure workflow:
- Customer deletion request (tenant wipe or API key purge) creates a deletion job and marks the tenant as inactive immediately.
- Primary storage purge: within 7 business days primary records (requests, outputs, cached artifacts) are removed from live storage and logical pointers are deleted.
- Backup lifecycle: backups are on a rolling retention: snapshots older than the backup retention window (default 90 days) are overwritten or pruned during normal maintenance. If a customer requires backups to be removed sooner, we require a contractual change and, depending on the snapshot schedule, may need up to one snapshot cycle (<=30 days) to fully expire older copies.
- Audit trail: per-request audit entries are preserved for 365 days for compliance; these records contain metadata (timestamps, tenant id, operation performed) but do not contain full request payloads after the purge.
- Evidence: upon completion we can provide a deletion certificate (signed log entry and job id) and the associated audit id for verification.

4) Encryption and key management: all data at rest and in transit is encrypted using AES-256. For hosted customers Redwood manages KMS keys by default; enterprise customers can opt for customer-managed keys (CMKs) where supported. Backups are encrypted with the same KMS configuration as the primary snapshot store.

5) Customer-facing phrasing (suggestion):
Short answer (one line): "Redwood stores hosted API request and response data in a single region you select; by default we retain payloads and short-term logs for 30 days and audit logs for 365 days; customers can request EU-only residency and submit tenant deletion requests which will purge primary data within 7 business days and expire backups per the configured backup retention window."

One-paragraph explanation: "Redwood Inference persists request and response data in the region selected at account creation to support debugging, monitoring, and security investigations. Default retention is 30 days for request/response payloads and 365 days for audit logs; backups are retained 90 days. Customers may elect EU-only residency and can request a tenant-level deletion, which triggers a purge of primary storage within 7 business days — backups are governed by the configured snapshot retention and will be pruned on the normal backup lifecycle. We provide a deletion certificate and audit identifiers upon completion for verification. For customers requiring shorter retention or accelerated backup deletion, enterprise contractual terms are available."

Notes / operational caveats:
- "Deletion certificate" contains job id, timestamp, and audit id; it is not a copy of deleted payloads.
- Some third-party backup providers may maintain rolling immutable snapshots; accelerated deletion in those cases requires contractual steps.
- For EU-only residency we recommend ordering within your procurement flow so the account is provisioned correctly at creation.

Michael — I left a couple of infra-level timing notes as comments in the spreadsheet for retention/backup windows; please confirm the 7-business-day primary purge SLA and the 90-day default backup retention.

— Irene

Hi Alice —

Thanks for sending the questionnaire — please find our consolidated answers below and attached a short spreadsheet + diagram for your records. If you need this language placed into a formal addendum or require customer-managed keys / accelerated backup deletion, we can add that to the agreement and coordinate procurement.

Summary (customer-friendly):
• Region / residency: Hosted accounts are provisioned to a single region selected at setup. We can provision EU-only residency (eu-west-1) upon request with an account-level configuration and SLA addendum.
• Retention: Default hosted retention is 30 days for request and response payloads and short-term logs, 365 days for audit logs, and 90 days for backup snapshots. Enterprise customers may request shorter retention windows.
• Deletion process: A tenant deletion request marks the tenant inactive and triggers a purge of primary storage within 7 business days. Backups are pruned according to the backup retention window (default 90 days); removal from backups may therefore take up to the configured snapshot cycle unless contractual changes are applied. We provide a deletion certificate and audit id upon completion.
• Encryption & keys: Data in transit and at rest is encrypted; hosted customers use Redwood-managed KMS by default; customer-managed KMS is available for enterprise customers.
